campaign.name: Dormant Card Reactivation — Explanation Test
campaign.description: Targets credit cards with no transaction in the last 90 days, on an Active account and Active card. Since the bank does not yet know why these cards went quiet, the journey runs a controlled test of two theories — forgetting vs. no reason to prefer the card — rather than guessing one. Within each theory, people who read the first message but don't act get a different argument; people who don't read it get a repeat on a different channel. Entry stays one door for everyone eligible; nothing is pre-segmented since no pattern was reported.

issuer.reference: tenant "TEN-IBL" selected in the UI before the conversation; the platform asserts it maps to issuer "IndusInd Bank (IBL)", which is a known application issuer. Issuer-dependent functionality (e.g. Smart Tags) resolves against this.

id.reference: Agent-namespaced temporary identifier, not a value the Drip Campaign system issued or persisted. The real campaign id is owned by the application and is minted when the campaign is actually created. There is no import path, so nothing here has been persisted anywhere.

description.reference: agent-written summary; states that fields may be unresolved

applyToAllPrograms.reference: Deliberate STARTING configuration for this prototype: all current and future programs are in scope. Expressed with the model's own applyToAllPrograms flag rather than a program list. Not evidence-backed, and not the application's own default — the application defaults this to false (DripBuilder.tsx:89). The user can review and change the program scope before the campaign goes live.

programs.reference: Empty as part of the same all-programs starting configuration: the model ignores `programs` when applyToAllPrograms is true (DripCampaign comment, graphTypes.ts), so no program list is fabricated. The user can narrow the scope to specific programs before the campaign goes live. Note: scenario.simulatedAnswers.which_programs names a fictional program and is not used.

root.reference: journey graph built by the planner through the application's own dcConfirmAddNode

controlPct.reference: The application's own default for a new campaign is 10 (DripBuilder.tsx:91 `useState(initial?.controlPct ?? 10)`). Required by the model, so it cannot be omitted. The agent does not design a holdout — this is stamped onto the canvas. Deliberately NOT presented as a bank-backed recommendation: softPreferences.preferredControlGroupPct is INVENTED and holds the same number by coincidence. Whether 10 is right for this campaign is a quality question for a reviewer.

status.reference: DRAFT — the only honest status while no import path exists. Activation is not the agent's to decide.

startDate.reason: No campaign objective window, no preparation lead time, and no real event calendar. The prototype's eventsCalendar is tagged INVENTED and is not evidence. Dates are left for a person to set.

guardrails.reference: DNC and NPA are exclusion lists on the campaign, checked at every node (DripCampaign.guardrails). The builder default is both on (DripBuilder.tsx:95-96). The agent does not design them — they are stamped so the canvas matches a hand-built campaign.

allowReEntry.reason: A campaign-level user choice. The UI defaults it to false (DripBuilder.tsx:92), but no user input or explicitly adopted default supports emitting it here. Omitted rather than hardcoded.

reEntryCooloffDuration.reason: Only meaningful when allowReEntry is true, which is itself unresolved. No cool-off is invented.

approach: Manager confirmed the goal is one transaction, not sustained spend, and success is counted as number of dormant cards reactivated, not value — first time running this, so no benchmark exists (user).
Manager does not know who already comes back on their own, and does not know why the rest stay dormant — both recorded as unknown rather than guessed as fact (user, basis 'not sure').
Manager has not seen a pattern on card age, limit, or auto-debit presence either (user, 'not really') — so the entry stays one door for everyone eligible; no segment is assumed.

Since the reason for dormancy is unknown, the plan tests it rather than guessing it, using two different theories of why the card went quiet — forgetting vs. no reason to prefer the card over UPI/other options (tool: market knowledge on UPI dominance is verified, not invented).
No risk appetite was stated, so per guidance an unstated appetite means include a real test and don't thin the plan (platform guidance).

Transaction-absence entry and the transaction goal both rely on a Transaction event category the platform lists as proposed, not yet confirmed built in production (tool: list_event_types) — flagged as a limitation, not hidden.
assumptions: Any genuine transaction (not a fee, reversal or system-generated entry) counts as reactivation, since the manager said 'at least one transaction again' without qualification.
Only Active accounts and Active cards are targeted; closed, charged-off or blocked cards are excluded even though the manager didn't say so, since messaging them would be pointless or non-compliant.
WhatsApp is the right first touch for reach in this market per the knowledge base, not chosen for cost.
unknowns: Whether the Transaction event category actually fires in production for this tenant — it is listed as proposed, not confirmed built.
Which of the two dormancy theories actually explains more of the dormant base — this run is designed to produce that evidence, not assume it.
designWarnings: This experiment says it tests explanation, but Reminder (forgot-the-card theory) and Benefit-led (no-reason-to-switch-back theory) are the same journey — same contacts, same channels, same spacing. Only the words differ, so whichever arm wins, it cannot tell you which barrier was real.
strategy.summary: You told me reactivation means at least one transaction again, that success is counted as the number of dormant cards that come back (not spend value), and that this is the first time you're running this \u2014 so there's no benchmark to measure against. Since the 'why' is genuinely unknown, this plan doesn't guess at a single message \u2014 it runs one eligibility track for every dormant card and tests two real theories against each other and against the built-in holdout.
